sentences.span: The binding constraint on AI infrastructure is power and grid access.
sentences.why: Matches MS's framing (also echoed via an On Semiconductor quote in 19893: 'the bottleneck moves to power... from grid to site to core') that power, not chip supply, is the gating factor through the 2026-28/29 forecast window.

sentences.span: we sized the US data center power shortfall at 57 GW from 2026-28. We forecast this is 32 GW net of time to power solutions... Net of innovative 'time to power' solutions, we project that US data center developers will face a 32-42GW Shortfall through 2028, 34-43% of demanded power.
sentences.why: All figures (57 GW gross, 32 GW net, 32-42 GW shortfall range, 34-43%) match exactly.

sentences.span: we move our US share of global compute to 55% from 60% previously... While we expect international [capacity to grow]
sentences.why: Exact match on the 60%-to-55% revision, and the source goes on to say international expansion doesn't have enough capacity to absorb the US shortfall, supporting the 'overseas expansion does not solve the domestic shortage' clause.

sentences.span: the still durable bull case of compute demand outstripping compute supply (in turn, driving confidence in 2027+ capex)
sentences.why: Direct match to Goldman's (Callahan desk) framing of the durable bull case and its link to 2027+ capex confidence.

sentences.span: Nvidia confirmed our thesis that there is not enough power to meet demand, and there are more semiconductors being built than there are places to put them.
sentences.why: Morgan Stanley's reading of the identical demand/supply gap: the chips (demand signal) exist but power infrastructure can't yet serve them, which is paraphrased faithfully as 'evidence of demand the industry cannot yet serve.'

sentences.span: TSM preview .. reports Thursday 10/15 (pre-market) .. sentiment remains upbeat, though, TSM did just turn in its biggest 4-day pullback since late-July (down ~7% Tues-Fri of this past week)
sentences.why: Exact match on date, pre-market timing, upbeat sentiment, ~7% four-day drop, and 'since late-July' comparison.

No source document ties a TSM/semis capex guidance walk-back to a 'power-constrained read' winning. 19902's debate is framed as whether management gives 2027 capex visibility at all, not a power-vs-demand framing; 19893's only 'power-constrained' usage is about ASICs losing share to GPUs, unrelated to guidance outcomes. This reads as the pulse's own synthesized invalidation line, not a sourced claim.

sentences.span: Our Morgan Stanley Thematics team forecasts 160 GW of incremental data center power demand from 2026-2029, 22 GW of which are already under construction and have a power grid connection. We also estimate 36 GW of available US grid capacity... there is 23 GW of BTM power generation equipment that has been procured... This leaves a 77 GW shortfall
sentences.why: All figures match exactly: 160 GW, 22 GW under construction with grid connection, and the 77 GW residual shortfall after grid capacity (36 GW) and already-procured BTM equipment (23 GW) are netted out.

sentences.span: Incorporating these factors alongside SCACP, Bloom Energy's SOFC ranks #1, BorgWarner's Turbine Generator #2 and FTAI's Aeroderivative solution #3... Top ideas for onsite power equipment suppliers: Bloom Energy (BE), Baker Hughes (BKR), BorgWarner (BWA...), Cummins (CMI), ERock (EROC), FTAI Aviation (FTAI), INNIO (INIO), and Rolls [Royce]
sentences.why: Ranking order and full equipment-ideas list match exactly; SCACP (Stranded Compute Adjusted Cost of Power) is defined in the source as adding the cost of idle/stranded compute waiting on power.

sentences.span: Sunrun and Tesla coordinated more than 140,000 residential batteries to deliver over 580 MW of peak power to the California grid for a three-hour evening dispatch. Of that capacity, 517 MW came from approximately 110,000 Tesla Powerwalls, while another 63 MW came from batteries made by other manufacturers.
sentences.why: Exact match on all figures (140,000 batteries, 580 MW, 517 MW/110,000 Powerwalls, 63 MW other manufacturers) and the California heat-wave context.

sentences.span: we expect the ESS market to grow from 57 GWh in 2025 to 280 GWh by 2030... Our US Clean Tech team projects net additions to the US energy-storage market to grow at a 38% CAGR from 2025-2030, reaching 279 GWh annual deployments by 2030.
sentences.why: Matches both figures the source gives for the same forecast (280 GWh vs 279 GWh is the source's own minor rounding variance, not a distortion), plus the 38% CAGR.

sentences.span: Since 1Q25 our estimate of the real neutral rate has risen from under 100bp to about 150bp, suggesting current policy is neutral or modestly restrictive.
sentences.why: Exact match on the real neutral rate's rise from under/just-under 100bp to about 150bp since 1Q25.

sentences.span: We forecast core CPI at 0.24% m/m in September (2.5%y/y), five basis points below August's 0.29% increase... We expect headline CPI at 0.62% m/m and 3.69% y/y, reflecting another sizable increase in gasoline prices.
sentences.why: Verbatim match on every figure: 0.24% core m/m, 2.5% y/y, five bp below August's 0.29%, 0.62% headline m/m, 3.69% y/y, gasoline driver.

sentences.span: Thursday 15 Oct... Retail Sales Advance m/m Sep 0.3... Retail Sales Ex Auto m/m Sep 0.5... Retail Sales Control Group Sep 0.2
sentences.why: Matches the forecast column exactly: 0.3% headline, 0.5% ex-auto, 0.2% control group, dated Oct 15.

sentences.span: Still, Sept CPI next week matters for the Oct meeting. We expect core CPI at 0.24% m/m, headline at 0.62%.
sentences.why: MS explicitly frames the CPI print as the swing factor for its two-more-hikes call; a hotter-than-forecast core reading is the natural condition that would upend that call, consistent with the bank's own stated stance.
